title: Error Budget Gating — Pilot Rollout Plan (warn-only → soft block → hard block)
linked_artifacts: Linear: ENG-2427 (pilot enforcement for API gateway + routing services)
GitHub: redwood/pull_request_18463 (release gate step + override token)
GitHub: perf-canary/pull_request_64 (canary analyzer consumes budget status)
Slack: #eng-platform thread_1737481203 (wiring budget checks into deploy tooling)
content:
Doc intent
- This is the pilot plan for tying error budget status to delivery workflows (deploys + rollouts) so teams feel budget burn.
- Pilot is intentionally narrow: a small set of services/routes, limited blast radius, and gradual gating modes.
- Output of pilot: (1) a stable budget-check API + CI integration pattern, (2) calibrated thresholds (noise vs signal), (3) an agreed exception/override workflow that doesn’t get abused.

Background / why this pilot
- We already page on incidents; budget burn should become a leading indicator that affects change velocity.
- We need to validate:
  - Budget calculations are correct enough for gating (no false blocks due to data issues).
  - Gating adds pressure in the right places (unsafe changes slow down; urgent fixes still ship).
  - Dedicated nuances are respected (don’t degrade Dedicated isolation with broad fallbacks).

Non-goals (pilot)
- Not changing customer SLAs/contract terms.
- Not enforcing gates for Redwood Private/on-prem.
- Not gating every deploy across the company; the pilot only targets a limited set of services + environments.

Pilot scope

Tiers included
- Hosted API: YES (primary pilot tier)
- Dedicated: PARTIAL (only “safe” Dedicated control-plane and routing components; no forced mitigations that violate pool isolation)
- Private: NO (document guidance only)

Services / systems in the pilot (phase 1 participants)
1) API Gateway (Hosted)
   - Owner: Amara Diallo
   - Why: close to customer SLI definitions (timeouts, 5xx, streaming disconnect attribution)
   - Deployment surface: frequent, high-impact

2) Control Plane (Hosted + Dedicated)
   - Owner: Ethan Park / Benji Okafor
   - Why: hosts the budget-check endpoint and policy hook; also involved in rollouts

3) Smart Routing / Policy Engine hooks (Hosted + Dedicated)
   - Owner: Mina Haddad / Jordan Lee
   - Why: can consult budget + burn signals and influence safe behavior (fallback vs freeze)

4) perf-canary integration (Hosted)
   - Owner: Paula Mendes / Jada Williams (product workflow), Devon Price (implementation)
   - Why: canary results should be annotated with budget risk; early “soft stop” mechanism

Explicitly out of pilot (for now)
- Serving runtime deploy gating (too many deploys; want to stabilize semantics first)
- Metrics ingestion pipeline changes (except what’s required to fix correctness)
- Any gating for customer-specific Dedicated pools beyond basic readiness SLI signal surfacing

Definitions used by gates (pilot-specific, to be revisited)
- “Budget remaining” is computed per {tier, service, region} and (where feasible) per {route group}.
- “Burn rate” follows the org standard multi-window approach (short + long window), but we will keep the pilot conservative to avoid flapping.
- Gate checks are always scoped. Example scope keys in pilot:
  - Hosted / api-gateway / us-east-1 / (chat-streaming)
  - Hosted / routing / eu-west-1 / (all)
  - Dedicated / control-plane / us-east-1 / (all)

Gate modes (what happens)
- Warn-only: deployment proceeds; gate posts warnings and links to dashboards/runbooks.
- Soft block: deployment requires explicit acknowledgement and oncall sign-off (lightweight) OR an override token.
- Hard block: deployment is blocked unless break-glass override token is used (and audited); typically only when budget is exhausted or burn is severe.

IMPORTANT: “hard block” is only for production deploys (and later for progressive rollout progression), not for staging/dev.

Rollout stages and timeline (proposed)

Stage 0 — Instrumentation + data validation (1–2 weeks)
Owner(s): Aisha Bello / Nadia Rahman for data correctness; Devon Price for pipeline integration
- Ensure budget-check endpoint returns a deterministic result for a given scope (no changing answers during a single pipeline run).
- Validate SLIs used in gating match SLO definitions (especially streaming TTFT vs stream duration + disconnect types).
- Create a “known false positive” list and a triage workflow.
Success criteria to exit stage 0
- <1% of gate checks fail due to internal errors/timeouts calling budget-check.
- Gate decision latency < 500ms p95 from CI runners.
- At least one week of budget computations backfilled for pilot services for comparison.

Stage 1 — Warn-only in CI for production deploy pipelines (2 weeks)
Owner(s): Sahana Iyer / Devon Price
Applies to
- API Gateway prod deploy pipeline
- Control Plane prod deploy pipeline
- Routing prod deploy pipeline
Behavior
- Always allow deploy.
- Post a structured message to the pipeline summary (and optionally Slack) including:
  - budget remaining (%)
  - burn rate status (ok / elevated / severe)
  - scope used
  - link to dashboard and error budget policy
- Record results in a log for later analysis (to measure how often we would have blocked).
Success criteria to exit stage 1
- Warnings are stable (no noisy flip-flops hour-to-hour for unchanged service).
- Teams confirm warnings are understandable (no “what does this mean?” every time).
- At least 2 real incidents where the warning correlates with an issue (qualitative validation).

Stage 2 — Soft block for a subset of deploys (2–4 weeks)
Owner(s): Connor O’Brien (change mgmt), Rafael Mendes (SRE), Ethan Park (control plane)
Applies to
- Hosted: API Gateway + Routing (production only)
- Dedicated: Control Plane only (production only)
Soft block triggers (pilot thresholds)
- Condition A: budget remaining < 25% AND long-window burn is elevated
- Condition B: short-window burn is severe (even if remaining is higher)
- Condition C: budget computation missing for required scope (treat as “degraded signal” → soft block, not hard)
Soft block behavior
- Deployment requires one of:
  1) “Acknowledge + link to mitigation plan” (freeform text in CI)
  2) Oncall sign-off (Slack approval in #eng-oncall, lightweight)
  3) Override token (see override section)
- The gate message must include “what to do next” (dashboards + runbook).
Success criteria to exit stage 2
- <10% of deploy attempts hit soft block unexpectedly (i.e., not known ongoing incident/burn).
- When soft-block occurs during real issues, it reduces change volume (less churn during incidents).
- Override usage is low and reviewed weekly (no “override as default”).

Stage 3 — Hard block for narrowly-scoped scenarios (2–4 weeks)
Owner(s): Sean Gallagher (policy owner), Connor O’Brien (governance), Jordan Lee (policy engine)
Applies to
- Hosted: API Gateway only, then Routing (production only)
- Dedicated: NO hard block during pilot (dedicated has higher operational sensitivity; we’ll revisit after readiness SLI stabilizes)
Hard block triggers (pilot thresholds)
- Condition A: budget exhausted (<= 0% remaining)
- Condition B: severe multi-window burn sustained for >30 minutes AND mitigation already in progress (to avoid blocking the fix we need)
Hard block behavior
- Block the deploy unless an override token is provided.
- If blocked, the CI output should suggest alternatives:
  - revert/cancel rollout
  - route fallback / protective throttling enablement (Hosted)
  - ship via “mitigation-only” pipeline (if we create this)

Stage 4 — Expand to progressive rollout gating (post-pilot)
- Goal: canary progression is stopped automatically when scoped budget is exhausted (or when burn is severe).
- Implementation is tied to perf-canary + rollout tooling UX; tracked separately but depends on pilot learnings.

Environments
- dev/staging: warn-only informational checks (no blocks)
- production: staged as described above

What exactly is being gated

A) CI deploy pipeline gate (primary)
- Before prod deploy is approved/executed, pipeline calls budget-check with:
  - tier
  - service
  - region
  - route_group (optional)
  - change_id (build SHA)
- Gate returns: allow / warn / soft_block / hard_block + reason codes.

B) Rollout progression gate (secondary / later)
- Canary analyzer consumes budget status and adds a “budget risk” annotation.
- In soft-block/hard-block modes: analyzer can stop progression.

C) Optional routing mitigation hook (NOT part of gating, but linked)
- If burn is severe, policy engine may prefer safer fallback behavior for Hosted (not Dedicated).

Override / exception handling (pilot)

Override token design (implementation in progress)
- Token is minted by control plane admin endpoint with TTL.
- Token scope: {tier, service, region} (must not be global).
- Token must include:
  - requester
  - approver
  - reason (freeform)
  - incident link (optional)
  - TTL (default 2 hours; max 24 hours)
- All overrides are logged and reviewable.

Who can approve overrides (pilot)
- For Hosted: platform-oncall OR SRE-oncall can approve.
- For Dedicated: dedicated-oncall OR SRE-oncall can approve.
- For high-risk changes (routing, gateway): require oncall approval; no “self-approve.”

Valid override reasons (pilot)
- Shipping a mitigation/fix that reduces burn or restores service.
- Shipping a rollback.
- Security incident / urgent compliance fix.
- False positive due to known metrics issue (must link to a ticket).

Invalid override reasons
- “Need to hit launch date” without mitigation.
- “It’s flaky but probably fine.”

Weekly review
- Platform eng + SRE review override log weekly during the pilot.
- If override usage spikes, we pause escalation to hard block.

Rollback plan (if gating causes harm)

Immediate rollback triggers
- Multiple false hard-blocks during incident response (blocking mitigations).
- Budget-check endpoint instability causing CI failures.
- Widespread “budget missing” due to pipeline/metrics changes.

Rollback actions (ordered)
1) Flip feature flag to revert hard/soft blocks → warn-only (same day)
2) If still unstable, disable gate step entirely in CI templates (same day)
3) Roll back budget-check endpoint changes if they are the instability source (within 24h)

Rollback owner / decision maker
- Oncall can flip to warn-only.
- SRE Director (Sean Gallagher) + VP Eng Platform (Priya Natarajan) decide on full disablement if it impacts multiple teams.

Monitoring the pilot (what we measure)
- Gate health
  - % of CI runs where budget-check call succeeds
  - latency of gate check
- Noise
  - soft-block/hard-block count per day
  - block reason distribution
- Impact
  - change volume during incidents (before vs after)
  - regression rate after deploys (proxy: incident count/SEVs tied to pilot services)
- Human process
  - override count, TTLs, and reasons
  - “time-to-approval” for soft-block scenarios

Open questions / TODOs
- Streaming routes: do we scope gating to TTFT SLI only for streaming, or include disconnect rate as separate trigger?
- Dedicated: should we include dedicated pool readiness SLI as a gating input, or keep it informational until it stabilizes?
- “Mitigation-only pipeline” idea: a deployment path that is always allowed if it matches certain labels (e.g., rollback, config-only throttle). Worth it?
- Missing data handling: soft block vs warn-only when the budget computation job is behind.

Next steps
- Sahana/Devon: finalize CI step integration in API gateway + routing pipelines (warn-only).
- Aisha/Nadia: confirm pilot SLI query correctness and create a short “known edge cases” page for oncall.
- Connor: publish lightweight oncall sign-off procedure for soft blocks (template message + what to check).
- Ethan/Benji: ensure override minting is audited and usable from incident channels.

Appendix: pilot contact points

- Control plane: Ethan Park, Benji Okafor
